chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man who digs a well in his house or on his land. He said: “As for what he dug in his own property, there is no liability upon him. But as for what he dug in the road or in other than what he owns, then he is liable for whatever falls into it.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرَ: a well that is dug into the ground
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: legal liability or responsibility for damage

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if someone falls into a well he dug on his property or in a public الطريق?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding liability for harm caused by digging a well. If a person digs on his own property, he bears no guarantee, but if he digs in a public road or on property he does not own, he is responsible for what falls into it.
